beats.say: Paris streets buzz as Napoleon III signs the secret decree to modernize the army in early 1869.
He orders the construction of ironclad warships, believing steel hulls will outmatch any rival navy.
Meanwhile, the emperor covertly funds the secret society of French engineers to build a massive telegraph line across the Rhine.
In 1870, he ignores warnings from General Trochu, insisting the Prussian army is still disorganized.
The emperor's private diary reveals he believed the French cavalry could break any infantry line with sheer speed.
But his overconfidence blinds him to the newly deployed Krupp breech-loading rifles that out-range French muskets.
When the Battle of Sedan arrives, his secret telegraph line fails, leaving Paris in darkness.
The emperor flees to Versailles, hoping the opulent palace will mask his shattered empire.
In exile, he writes a manifesto claiming the war was a test of French industrial might, not politics.
History remembers his hubris, but the hidden telegraph project sparked the first modern European communications network.
